:::{#exm-poisson-log-partition-variance}
#### The variance of the Poisson distribution from its log-partition function

<!-- no-figure: the example compares two numbers computed from the same data -->

In @exm-poisson-log-partition-mean,
the log-partition function is $\logpartitionf{\natparam} = \expf{\natparam}$,
and the [statistic](sufficiency.qmd#def-statistic) is $\statf{\rvar} = \rvar$.
By @thm-log-partition-variance,

$$
\Var{\Rvar}
= \Var{\statf{\Rvar}}
= \dif{^2 \logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam^2}
= \expf{\natparam}.
$$

Since $\expf{\natparam} = \rate$,
we have $\Var{\Rvar} = \rate$,
the [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance)
of the [Poisson distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson).

To check @thm-log-partition-variance on data,
we compute its two sides separately for the cyclone counts of @exm-poisson-exponential-family,
with $\rate$ set to the [sample mean](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-mean).
The left side adds $\sqf{\rvar - \rate} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \rate}$ over the counts from 0 to 100,
and the right side is a second central difference of $\logpartitionf{\natparam}$ at $\natparam = \logf{\rate}$.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: poisson-log-partition-variance-r
#| code-fold: false
cyclones <- c(6, 5, 4, 6, 6, 3, 12, 7, 4, 2, 6, 7, 4)
rate <- mean(cyclones)
natural_parameter <- log(rate)

counts <- 0:100
squared_deviations <- (counts - rate)^2
weighted_deviations <- squared_deviations * dpois(counts, rate)
variance_statistic <- sum(weighted_deviations)

log_partition <- exp
step <- 1e-4
log_partition_up <- log_partition(natural_parameter + step)
log_partition_mid <- log_partition(natural_parameter)
log_partition_down <- log_partition(natural_parameter - step)
second_diff <- log_partition_up - 2 * log_partition_mid + log_partition_down
second_derivative <- second_diff / step^2

tibble::tibble(variance_statistic, second_derivative)
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: poisson-log-partition-variance-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import poisson

cyclones = np.array([6, 5, 4, 6, 6, 3, 12, 7, 4, 2, 6, 7, 4])
rate = cyclones.mean()
natural_parameter = np.log(rate)

counts = np.arange(0, 101)
squared_deviations = (counts - rate) ** 2
variance_statistic = np.sum(squared_deviations * poisson.pmf(counts, rate))

log_partition = np.exp
step = 1e-4
log_partition_up = log_partition(natural_parameter + step)
log_partition_mid = log_partition(natural_parameter)
log_partition_down = log_partition(natural_parameter - step)
second_diff = log_partition_up - 2 * log_partition_mid + log_partition_down
second_derivative = second_diff / step**2

pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "variance_statistic": [variance_statistic],
        "second_derivative": [second_derivative],
    }
)
```

:::

The two sides agree at `r round(variance_statistic, 3)`,
and differ by `r format(abs(variance_statistic - second_derivative), digits = 2)`.
That difference is numerical error,
from stopping the counts at 100 and from the finite step of the second difference.
:::
